newsitem.title: NIGERIA: African mission in Nigeria sees Saro-Wiwa's mother.
newsitem.headline: African mission in Nigeria sees Saro-Wiwa's mother.

text.p: An African team checking Nigerian human rights said they met military ruler General Sani Abacha and the mother of executed author Ken Saro-Wiwa during a week long visit which ended on Friday.
The three-member delegation apologised to local activists for its failure to meet them last Saturday.

"It was a matter of deep regret for members of the mission that inclement weather forced us to be driven by road to Abuja from Lagos while unknown to us as a result of poor communications a room bursting with representatives of NGOs were waiting for a meeting with us...We apologise profusely," the statement said.

The team, from the Gambia-based African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights has been largely shunned by local rights activists because it came after two UN investigators called off a similar trip when the military authorities denied them access to jails and detainees.

Ghanaian professor Victor Danqua, who led the three-man team, said they met Saro-Wiwa's mother in volatile Ogoniland where they also saw 19 youths from the Ogoni tribe awaiting trial for the same murders for which Saro-Wiwa and eight others were hanged.

"We visited Ogoni yesterday where we had discussions with Ken Saro-Wiwa's mother and the 19 Ogoni youths in detention," he told Reuters. "The meeting was fruitful, they were happy to meet with us and they narrated their plight which we also noted."
He said they also met military ruler Abacha behind closed doors in his Aso Rock villa, but gave no details.
The 19 have been detained since 1994 when four prominent chiefs were murdered in Ogoniland.
Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists were hanged for the murders the following year after a trial by a tribunal, provoking worldwide condemnation of Nigeria's military leaders.
"Their (Ogoni 19) concerns will be passed onto the appropriate authorities," their end-of-mission statement said.
The statement did not say if the delegation had succeeded in meeting Moshood Abiola, the businessman believed to have won Nigeria's annulled 1993 presidential election.
Abiola has been held in seclusion since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of the military rulers.
Abacha's government is implementing a programme to restore civil rule next year starting with municipal polls on Saturday.
